findings.text: claim_service() is applied but unguarded — the host refuses the -900 lowering so the service reads 0 whether or not the call runs, and the negative control at logs/negative-control-claim-removed.log removed only the two claim_worker calls, so the service side of the deliverable is not protected by any test.

service_outranks_worker has no caller in the tree and the test restates its predicate inline at tests/test_coordination_services_survive_a_full_job.py:118, so the module's rule that an unreadable reading answers False rather than a pass is never exercised.

the assertion compares the worker's reading against oom_priority.WORKER_OOM_SCORE_ADJUSTMENT, a constant the code under test also reads, so lowering both sides together leaves it green; only the second assertion there, `worker > 0`, is independent of that constant.

the after_suite value is not valid JSON — `"failure_count: 0}` is unquoted and unterminated — so a reader that parses the recorded arm pair cannot read the head arm's failure count and has to fall back to the log.

the header names revision 8863ecb4f36 while the tree it names is the node worktree carrying 3d2e5571 plus the mutation, so a reader who takes the revision line as the code measured reads the base revision as having been executed.

the Done when's two-hour, ten-minute-interval resident-memory measure under 1 GiB is recorded as not produced, leaving the delivered gate asserting only the ordering clause; the measure needs a separately dispatched node that opens the window.
